final_method_items.summary: Given a set of newly created SSA names (NEW_SSA_NAMES) and a set of existing SSA names (OLD_SSA_NAMES), update the SSA form so that: 1- The names in OLD_SSA_NAMES dominated by the definitions of NEW_SSA_NAMES are all re-written to be reached by the appropriate definition from NEW_SSA_NAMES. 2- If needed, new PHI nodes are added to the iterated dominance frontier of the blocks where each of NEW_SSA_NAMES are defined. The mapping between OLD_SSA_NAMES and NEW_SSA_NAMES is setup by calling create_new_def_for to create new defs for names that the caller wants to replace. The caller cretaes the new names to be inserted and the names that need to be replaced by calling create_new_def_for for each old definition to be replaced. Note that the function assumes that the new defining statement has already been inserted in the IL. For instance, given the following code: 1 L0: 2 x_1 = PHI (0, x_5) 3 if (x_1 < 10) 4 if (x_1 > 7) 5 y_2 = 0 6 else 7 y_3 = x_1 + x_7 8 endif 9 x_5 = x_1 + 1 10 goto L0; 11 endif Suppose that we insert new names x_10 and x_11 (lines 4 and 8). 1 L0: 2 x_1 = PHI (0, x_5) 3 if (x_1 < 10) 4 x_10 = ... 5 if (x_1 > 7) 6 y_2 = 0 7 else 8 x_11 = ... 9 y_3 = x_1 + x_7 10 endif

behavior_items: The reproducer is a compile-time failure only: GCC crashes while compiling, and there is no indication of a runtime misbehavior in user code. The failure is triggered by a specific optimization pipeline rather than by invalid source semantics.

The interesting option combination is -Os -flto -ffat-lto-objects -floop-parallelize-all -ftree-parallelize-loops=2 with dynamic scheduling. This forces GCC to consider automatic loop parallelization, emit LTO information, and then analyze compiler-generated helper functions during interprocedural optimization.

The diagnostic says the crash happens in the synthesized function foo0._loopfn.0. That naming pattern is typical of GCC's loop-parallelization pass: it outlines a loop body into a helper function that will be executed by worker threads or a runtime loop scheduler.

Because the ICE occurs in foo0._loopfn.0 rather than directly in the original source function, the reproducer exercises code generation for an outlined parallel loop body, not just ordinary scalar optimization of the original function.

The backtrace shows the crash site at bitmap_alloc in bitmap.cc, called from walk_aliased_vdefs_1 in tree-ssa-alias.cc. This means GCC is trying to allocate alias-analysis bookkeeping while walking virtual definitions of memory state in SSA form.

Virtual definitions represent memory side effects. So the outlined loop body likely contains memory accesses or calls that require the compiler to reason about aliasing and memory flow, and that reasoning is what reaches the failing path.

The next stack frame, ipa_polymorphic_call_context::get_dynamic_type, is notable because it is usually associated with computing object or memory-derived type information for calls during interprocedural propagation. Even though this is C code, that routine is part of generic IPA infrastructure and can still be reached while trying to characterize call arguments or memory-based context.

The crash therefore is not in the loop parallelizer itself at the moment it transforms the loop, but later when GCC performs IPA jump-function analysis on the newly created helper function and tries to inspect aliased memory definitions reachable from one of its statements.

The call chain ipa_compute_jump_functions_for_edge -> ipa_compute_jump_functions_for_bb -> ipa_analyze_node shows that GCC is analyzing call edges/basic blocks of the generated loop helper for interprocedural constant/context propagation. The reproducer exercises interaction between parloops-created functions and IPA analysis.

The presence of -flto and -ffat-lto-objects matters because LTO keeps richer whole-program IR and causes additional interprocedural processing. The bug report strongly suggests the helper function is inserted into the call graph and then reprocessed in a context where some bitmap/obstack state expected by alias analysis is missing or invalid.

The ICE in bitmap_alloc at a checking build location strongly suggests an internal invariant violation rather than simple out-of-memory. bitmap_alloc normally expects a valid bitmap obstack; the crash implies GCC reached alias-walking code with an uninitialized, null, or otherwise inconsistent bitmap allocation context.

The reproducer thus stresses a compiler corner case where a newly materialized outlined loop function is analyzed too early, too late, or without all analysis state being properly prepared. The symbol_table::process_new_functions frames support that interpretation because they show GCC handling newly added functions during compilation.

The use of -floop-parallelize-all is important because it aggressively parallelizes loops even when profitability is doubtful, increasing the chance that a reduced testcase produces a _loopfn helper and reaches uncommon analysis paths.

The use of --param=parloops-schedule=dynamic further pushes the compiler down a specific parallel-loop code path, likely changing the outlined helper's control flow or runtime API calls enough to expose the bug.

The fact that this is labeled a regression for GCC 15 indicates the reproducer likely compiled in earlier revisions or releases, so the exercised behavior is a recently broken interaction among loop outlining, SSA alias walking, and IPA/LTO analysis rather than a long-standing unsupported construct.

No evidence in the report suggests undefined behavior in the source is required. The reduced testcase appears intended solely to create a loop that GCC outlines and then analyzes; the failure is entirely inside compiler internals.

In practical terms, the reproducer checks whether GCC can safely create a parallel loop helper, register it in the call graph, and run interprocedural jump-function and alias analysis on it under LTO. The observed behavior is that this pipeline aborts with an ICE before code generation completes.
test_behavior_analysis.summary: The reproducer triggers a GCC 15 regression in the interaction between automatic loop parallelization and LTO-era IPA analysis. With aggressive parloops options enabled, GCC outlines a loop into a synthetic helper function named like foo0._loopfn.0. During later interprocedural analysis of that new function, GCC walks SSA virtual memory definitions for alias/type context computation, reaches walk_aliased_vdefs, and then crashes in bitmap_alloc because internal bitmap allocation state is inconsistent. So the code logic exercised is not unusual runtime behavior of the user program; it is the compiler pipeline for generating and then analyzing an outlined parallel-loop helper under -Os -flto -ffat-lto-objects -floop-parallelize-all, where the bug is an internal compiler invariant failure during IPA/alias processing of the synthesized function.

test_failure_analysis.analysis: The failure pattern points to a GCC middle-end regression in the interaction between loop parallelization outlining and later IPA/LTO analysis, not to a problem in the testcase source. The trigger requires GCC to synthesize a helper function named like foo0._loopfn.0 via the parloops pass, then immediately analyze that new function through callgraph insertion and IPA jump-function propagation under LTO. The backtrace shows the crash occurs when ipa_compute_jump_functions_for_edge invokes ipa_polymorphic_call_context::get_dynamic_type, which in turn walks aliased virtual defs in tree-ssa-alias. Hitting an ICE in bitmap_alloc from walk_aliased_vdefs strongly suggests alias-walking code was entered with invalid or unprepared bitmap allocation state, or with malformed SSA/alias metadata for the outlined helper. Common pattern: a newly created compiler-generated function containing memory side effects is being processed by IPA before all alias/SSA/context structures expected by walk_aliased_vdefs are initialized consistently. Because this is a GCC 15 regression and only appears with the specific -flto + parloops pipeline, the most likely defects are in production compiler code that wires together parloops-generated functions, cgraph insertion, SSA alias state, and IPA propagation.

Recent regression in ipa_polymorphic_call_context::get_dynamic_type or its callers causes alias queries on statements/functions for which memory context is not valid yet.
